official_sources: Tunbridge Wells Local Validation List review 2026

official_measurement_examples.name: National validity components
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government guidance states that a valid planning application requires a completed form, national information requirements, the correct fee and applicable local information requirements.

official_measurement_examples.name: Two-year local-list currency
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local information requirements affect validity only where they are on a formally adopted local list published on the authority website less than two years before submission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Statutory tests
official_measurement_examples.fact: A requested local item must be reasonable for the nature and scale of the proposal and relate to a matter reasonably considered material to determination.

official_measurement_examples.name: Article 12 dispute route
official_measurement_examples.fact: Where an applicant disputes a validation information request, the Development Management Procedure Order provides an Article 12 notice procedure; disagreement is not proof that the application is valid or invalid without that process.

official_measurement_examples.name: Review frequency
official_measurement_examples.fact: National guidance says a local validation list should be reviewed at least every two years; a historical checklist must not be silently treated as current.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 adopted example
official_measurement_examples.fact: Breckland adopted a new Local List on 1 May 2026, illustrating that current local requirements can change even when national requirements remain the same.

official_measurement_examples.name: Consultation versus adoption
official_measurement_examples.fact: A draft local-list consultation is not the same as an adopted validation list; current adopted and proposed requirements must remain separate.

official_measurement_examples.name: Validation versus merits
official_measurement_examples.fact: Validation means an application contains the information needed to enter determination; it is not planning permission, approval on the merits, title evidence or a development-yield result.

core_rules: valid application is not planning permission
validation is not approval on merits
national and local requirements remain distinct
local list must retain publication/adoption date
draft consultation list is not adopted list
local information request must satisfy statutory tests
Article12 dispute route must retain outcome context
correct fee is part of validity where applicable
validation does not prove infrastructure capacity
validation documents do not calculate parcel yield
old local checklist is not automatically current
local list requirements vary by proposal type scale and location
no parcel validation clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official GOV.UK, legislation and current English local-authority sources checked on 2026-07-26. 2025-2026 adopted/reviewed local lists were retained with national/local, adoption/consultation, statutory-test and validation/permission distinctions; no parcel promotion.
